original_question: For n >= 2 and d >= 3, can one find a homogeneous SL_n-invariant on C[e_1, ..., e_n]_{n(d-2)} whose nonvanishing locus contains, as a closed subset, the set U_n^{n(d-2)} of degree n(d-2) forms F such that F^perp intersected with C[z_1, ..., z_n]_{d-1} is n-dimensional and has a basis with nonvanishing resultant?
target_in_paper: The draft is targeting Open Problem 3.10 in §3.3, stated immediately after Proposition 3.9: to find, for all n ≥ 2 and d ≥ 3, a homogeneous SL_n-invariant on C[e_1, ..., e_n]_{n(d-2)} whose nonvanishing locus contains U_n^{n(d-2)} as a closed subset. This problem is introduced as a sufficient route to condition (C2) in Open Problem 3.2, which is part of the strategy toward Conjecture 1.1. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1803.04005))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper-faithful core very well: the universal quantifiers n ≥ 2 and d ≥ 3; the ambient space C[e_1, ..., e_n]_{n(d-2)}; the requirement that the desired object be a homogeneous SL_n-invariant; and the exact geometric condition that U_n^{n(d-2)} be a closed subset of the invariant's nonvanishing locus. It also correctly describes U_n^{n(d-2)} using the degree-(d-1) piece of the apolar annihilator and the existence of a basis with nonvanishing resultant. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1803.04005))
missing_details: The paper works over the field C (more generally over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, but the survey is stated over C), so the stand-alone question should specify that ambient field. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1803.04005))

It should say explicitly that C[e_1, ..., e_n]_{n(d-2)} denotes the vector space of homogeneous forms of degree n(d-2) in the variables e_1, ..., e_n, with e_1, ..., e_n the standard basis of C^n. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1803.04005))

The notation F^perp should be defined via the apolar/differentiation action: F^perp = {h in C[z_1, ..., z_n] : h(∂/∂e_1, ..., ∂/∂e_n)F = 0}. The draft leaves this implicit. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1803.04005))

The degree condition in the annihilator should be written exactly as F^perp ∩ C[z_1, ..., z_n]_{d-1}; the paper uses degree d-1 because U_n^{n(d-2)} is the image of Ψ from complete intersections of type (d-1, ..., d-1). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1803.04005))

The phrase 'has a basis with nonvanishing resultant' should be read as: that n-dimensional subspace admits a basis of n forms of degree d-1 in z_1, ..., z_n whose resultant is nonzero. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1803.04005))

To match the paper exactly, the sought invariant should be called a homogeneous SL_n-invariant J on the space C[e_1, ..., e_n]_{n(d-2)}, and the conclusion should be phrased as 'U_n^{n(d-2)} is a closed subset of the complement to the zero locus of J.' ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1803.04005))

The draft does not mention the immediate context: this is posed after Proposition 3.9 because such a J is sufficient to obtain condition (C2), not because the paper proves an equivalence. That contextual role should be noted in the explanation, though not forced into the question itself. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1803.04005))
refined_question:
For every pair of integers n ≥ 2 and d ≥ 3, does there exist a homogeneous SL_n(C)-invariant polynomial J on the vector space C[e_1, ..., e_n]_{n(d-2)} of degree-n(d-2) forms such that the locus
U_n^{n(d-2)} := {F in C[e_1, ..., e_n]_{n(d-2)} : F^perp ∩ C[z_1, ..., z_n]_{d-1} is n-dimensional and admits a basis with nonzero resultant},
where F^perp = {h in C[z_1, ..., z_n] : h(∂/∂e_1, ..., ∂/∂e_n)F = 0},
is a closed subset of the complement of the zero locus of J? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1803.04005))
justification: The draft does not primarily target Conjecture 1.1 itself, but rather the more specific later open problem that the paper singles out as a way to verify condition (C2) in the GIT strategy for Conjecture 1.1. The exact match is Open Problem 3.10 in §3.3, and the surrounding context needed to make it stand-alone comes from the definition of U_n^{n(d-2)} in §2 and from Proposition 3.9, which explains why the existence of such an invariant would suffice for condition (C2). Since Proposition 3.9 gives only a sufficient condition, not an equivalence, no alternate equivalent formulation should be supplied. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1803.04005))
